pl-l4d27c3-d1e115.summary: States that the efficient cause of marriage is consent, not any consent, but expressed in words, and of the present, not the future.
claims: Marriage is caused by expressed consent of the present.

pl-l4d27c3-d1e118.summary: Explains: consent to the future, 'I will take you as husband and I you as wife', does not effect marriage; consent in mind not expressed in words or certain signs does not effect it; but if expressed in words though not willed in heart, absent coercion or fraud, the obligation of words 'I take you as husband and I you as wife' makes marriage.
claims: Future consent and unexpressed consent do not make marriage.
Expressed present consent binds, absent coercion or fraud.

pl-l4d27c3-d1e128.summary: Announces that the testimonies below prove that consent makes marriage.

pl-l4d27c3-d1e137.summary: Cites Pope Nicholas: according to the laws, the consent of those whose union is in question suffices; if it is lacking, all else, even intercourse, is in vain.
claims: Without consent, even intercourse does not make marriage.

pl-l4d27c3-d1e143.summary: Cites Chrysostom: not intercourse but will makes marriage, so separation of bodies does not dissolve it.

pl-l4d27c3-d1e149.summary: Cites Ambrose: not the deflowering of virginity but the conjugal pact makes marriage.

pl-l4d27c3-d1e159.summary: Concludes that consent, the conjugal pact, makes marriage, and from then it is marriage, whether or not carnal union preceded or follows.
claims: Marriage exists from consent, independent of consummation.

pl-l4d27c3.summary: The efficient cause of marriage is consent, expressed in words, and of the present, not the future: promising future marriage does not make it, nor does unexpressed consent; but words of present consent, without coercion or fraud, make marriage even if the heart does not will it. Isidore, Nicholas, Chrysostom, and Ambrose confirm that consent, the conjugal pact, makes marriage, not intercourse or deflowering. So marriage exists from consent, whether or not carnal union precedes or follows.
claims: The efficient cause of marriage is consent expressed in words of the present.
Consent to future marriage does not make marriage.
Expressed consent binds even if the heart dissents, absent coercion or fraud.
